# RelaySwarm

> Experimental peer-assisted HLS video delivery with WebRTC data channels,
> Nostr relay rendezvous, author-signed segment commitments and an hls.js
> loader. A separate native Node path uses HyperDHT and Noise. MIT licensed;
> v0.3.0 is the experimental prerelease; production acceptance remains open.

The canonical repository is https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm. Node 22.13+
is required; CI uses Node 24. Public distribution includes an installable
GitHub tarball, a standalone browser ESM bundle, the optional WASM module, native core
archives and SHA-256 checksums. The
source demo runs with `npm run demo`; synthetic media needs ffmpeg/libx264.

The original WebRTC CLI signs plaintext SDP and uses a digest supplied by its
seeder. The browser loader and shared session wire version 3 use pairwise
NIP-44-encrypted signals; the native path encrypts dial authorisation and uses
Noise for transfer. Package version 0.3.0, session version 3, commitment schemas
1/2/3 (3 experimental) and metrics version 2 are distinct. Published Swift RelaySwarmKit v0.5.0
supports wire version 3 and signed media, with actual SDK/Chrome loopback proof;
physical Apple-device and public-NAT compatibility remain unverified.

Browser modes are off (origin-only), shadow (origin playback plus extra sampled
peer traffic) and peer-first (verified peer bytes within a deadline, then normal
HTTP fallback). Uploading defaults to off and requires viewer opt-in. Peer-first
also requires a trusted signed kind-30311 event with the experimental
redistribution tag and an author or scoped-delegate signed commitment. The host selects
the stream, relays and ICE policy. The trusted-event adapter in v0.2.1 queries
through a bounded host callback with explicit author/origin/relay allowlists;
it does not adopt event-selected services or establish publisher trust.
Native HyperDHT cannot run in an ordinary browser page.

The publisher keeps its key in Node and signs only matching local full-segment
playlist contexts, including exact byte ranges and discontinuities. The player
has upload limits, an origin-only kill switch and locally downloaded receipts.
Viewer keys are ephemeral; participation is pseudonymous, and peers can learn network
addresses. Origin-only avoids swarm participation. No managed TURN/super-peer service, accepted RelaySwarm NIP or durable media
storage is supplied. Hosts can pass TURN credentials through explicit ICE policy.
The demo has an optional server-owned renewal adapter, off by default; it
preserves consent and spend on new credentials and keeps the original lease
when a cached reply repeats the same material. Expiry requires fresh Apply.
Current source optionally persists a private publisher identity, caches verified
file hashes/signatures, limits cumulative media upload, measures peer choice and
provides authenticated operator policy, bounded admission and durable idempotent
opt-in numeric reports. Upload budgets persist across reloads/tabs without consent.
Optional Nostr or host website accounts share a private durable allowance across
devices; account changes leave uploading off until fresh consent. The dated
pilot evidence records Nostr sign-in; integrating websites supply their own account resolver.
Wider media includes fMP4, audio, explicit AES-128, mixed variants and warm LL parts/deltas.
The example origin adds bounded blocking reload for compatible complete live
playlists across all renditions, with 24 waiters inside 32 media requests.
Raw media, peer deadlines and playback holdback are unchanged. One injected
loopback pair passed both qualities and restart with the option on and off;
recoverable playlist 503s occurred only with it on. Reliability improvement and
ordinary public/physical acceptance remain unproved.
The v0.2.1 supervised broadcast bridge creates two live HLS renditions and
can forward H.264/AAC separately to RTMPS with explicit TLS verification.
These additions are in v0.2.1 and absent from v0.1.0 downloads.
The source app and waiting listener use a 130-second HTTP keep-alive timeout
to outlast Caddy's default 120-second upstream idle pool. Ten-second request
and header deadlines and 128 connections remain bounded. A real 121-second
same-socket regression passes close/handover; distributed repair is unproved.

Desktop Chrome regressions and a short twelve-viewer loopback soak are recorded;
they do not establish physical-phone, varied-NAT or sustained operation readiness.
Peer-first media loads/bytes avoided are not net connection-data savings, and
upload counters measure committed media payload rather than acknowledged delivery.
Pending durable reservations can consume quota without entering those counters.
Documentation on main can include corrections after the immutable releases.
v0.3.0 adds the opt-in Rust/WASM core, experimental schema 3 piece commitments
and multi-holder transfers, UniFFI Swift/Kotlin bindings, advisory peer supply
hints and receipt switch-cost reporting. Core bindings do not include a native
WebRTC adapter or client. RelaySwarmKit has not adopted this core. The scheduler
retains the 32 KiB/s cold floor and at most three holders.

Production acceptance remains open. Dated pilot records retain their exact
sources and RED/open sustained-operation, physical-device, difficult-network
and net-benefit gates. This release does not deploy or qualify the pilot.
See the P01-P12 checklist and dated status evidence.

## Documentation

- [Experimental real-time transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/REALTIME-TRANSPORT.md): Source-only unordered datagram adapter over existing NIP-44 sessions; not a call SDK, SFU or managed service.
- [Native real-time operator backend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/NATIVE-REALTIME.md): Optional injected native initiator; the browser verifies remote channel reliability. Separately MPL-2.0 dependency, with macOS loopback evidence and WAN qualification still required.
- [Goals and agent handover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/AGENT-GOALS.md): Agreed P01-P12 goals, latest retained deployment evidence, remaining acceptance sequence and local evidence paths for a continuing agent.
- [Production features](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-FEATURES.md): Implemented source features, trust boundaries and native fallback.
- [Production delivery requirements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md): Full implementation, publication, deployment and real-world acceptance scope.
- [Protocol draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/NIP-DRAFT.md): Session v3, commitments, delegation and independent-client compatibility evidence.

- [Project overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/README.md): Scope, transport comparison, demo, release and commands.
- [Documentation index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/README.md): Routes for installation, integration, security and evidence.
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md): Exact tarball, pinned Git, bundle, checksums and source-demo instructions.
- [hls.js integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/INTEGRATION.md): Options, callbacks, consent, admission, metrics, commitments and stop semantics.
- [API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/API.md): Module exports; browser, publisher, relay/session and native primitives. Experimental opt-in peer supply hints allow origin-sustainable ABR ties only.
- [Publisher/player field test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FIELD-TEST.md): Supported HLS subset, HTTPS trials, local receipts and device/network gates.
- [Spry TURN interoperability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/interop/spry-turn.md): Forced relay-only HLS tests with the public v0.2.1 binary and separate viewer credentials. UDP passed; TCP/TLS carried verified media but missed the timing gate; TLS also lacked an active selected path at the final sample. Earlier shared-principal quota errors are documented; loopback only.
- [Broadcasting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/BROADCASTING.md): OBS/RTMP bridge, two-rendition HLS, persistent identity and separate optional RTMPS forwarding.
- [Operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md): Private state, authenticated policy/status, upload consent, numeric reporting and recovery.
- [Shared upload allowance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/ACCOUNT-UPLOAD-BUDGET.md): Durable allowance across devices, Nostr or host website authentication, explicit linking and controlled Chrome acceptance; deployed pilot offers Nostr, with owner/physical acceptance open.
- [Container pilot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/deploy/README.md): Isolated existing-server deployment, SSH ingest, HTTPS, health checks and rollback.
- [Native transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/NATIVE-TRANSPORT.md): HyperDHT/Noise protocol, one-use authorisation and trust/fallback boundaries.
- [Threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md): Implemented integrity/resource/privacy boundaries and outstanding adversarial work.
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/FAQ.md): Distribution, encryption, phones, infrastructure, consent and measurement answers.

## Evidence and maintenance

- [Evidence and remaining work](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/STATUS.md): Dated release, CI/soak measurements, distribution proof, deterministic silent-holder deadline classifications and unverified gates.
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/CHANGELOG.md): Shared-core v0.3.0 changes and published release history.
- [Maintaining the docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/MAINTAINING-DOCS.md): AI-context generation, link/freshness checks and public metadata.

## Optional

- [Core signature budget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/CORE-SIGNATURE-BUDGET.md): Dated compressed asset and actual Chrome verification measurements; an isolated prototype, with no production verifier change.
- [Native core packaging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/CORE-PACKAGING.md): Tag-gated release attachments and dispatch-only native build artefacts, checksums and source verification; source-bound assets and an unchanged local-path Swift package.

- [Full documentation context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/llms-full.txt): Generated maintained guides with absolute links; larger than the index.
- [Landscape](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/docs/LANDSCAPE.md): Primary-source comparison with other rendezvous/media projects.
- [Historical spike results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/spikes/RESULTS.md): Dated fixtures and measured topology; early PoCs have different trust assumptions.
- [Coding-agent guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgesworn/relayswarm/main/AGENTS.md): Local repository conventions and verification commands.
